The state is \(|\alpha\rangle \propto (1+i)|\uparrow\rangle + (2-i)|\downarrow\rangle\). Its norm squared is \(|1+i|^2 + |2-i|^2 = 2 + 5 = 7\), so the normalized state is \(|\alpha\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\big[(1+i)|\uparrow\rangle + (2-i)|\downarrow\rangle\big]\).

The operator \(A\) has matrix representation \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & \hbar/2 \\ \hbar/2 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\) in the \(\{|\uparrow\rangle, |\downarrow\rangle\}\) basis. This is \(A = \frac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_x\). Its eigenstates and eigenvalues are:
\[
|a_+\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|\uparrow\rangle + |\downarrow\rangle), \quad \text{eigenvalue } +\hbar/2
\]
\[
|a_-\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|\uparrow\rangle - |\downarrow\rangle), \quad \text{eigenvalue } -\hbar/2
\]

The probability amplitudes are:
\[
\langle a_+|\alpha\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{14}}\big[(1+i) + (2-i)\big] = \frac{3}{\sqrt{14}} \quad\Rightarrow\quad P(+) = \frac{9}{14} \approx 0.64
\]
\[
\langle a_-|\alpha\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{14}}\big[(1+i) - (2-i)\big] = \frac{-1+2i}{\sqrt{14}} \quad\Rightarrow\quad P(-) = \frac{5}{14} \approx 0.36
\]

The expectation value is \(\langle A \rangle = \frac{\hbar}{2}\big(P(+) - P(-)\big) = \frac{\hbar}{2}\left(\frac{9}{14} - \frac{5}{14}\right) = \frac{\hbar}{7}\).

These match option (B).

Answer: B
